accent-hot.displayName: Hot Red (focus, live, a filter that is on, a text action on hover)

on-accent-ink.displayName: White Ink on Flat Red, large text only

rule.displayName: Row Rule (13% white): under a .field row in the sheets and the NextStep lists

paper.displayName: Paper (white 94%): prints, slips, cards on the black table

tape.displayName: Tape (white 82%): a typed label over a print or a group

paper-ink-dim.displayName: Dim Paper Ink (black 66%, 5.3:1 on paper; edges, roles, states)

display.purpose: A poster title a step under the section head (--fs-display): the home event title and "Newsletter", the /venue address and "The entrance", the FAQ categories, "Become a partner", "Press kit".

headline.purpose: Every Closer title, the live ticket slip's name and price, the /team end title, the menu panel's primary links >=901px: --fs-h2 clamp(2.25rem, min(6vw, 9svh), 5.5rem).

head.purpose: A compact head on a card (--fs-head clamp(2.1rem, 3.4vw, 3rem)): the /contact index-card titles, the /venue card titles, the partnerships contact's name.

lede.purpose: Section ledes and status prose; the home facts note and newsletter lede.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono records figures: the ticket slip's date stamp and company figure, the FAQ index numbers, agenda break times. Never a word-label (the darkroom edges that set words in mono are an open point).

label-lg.purpose: The larger mono figure: the NextStep index, the agenda time gutter, the invite meta line.

label-xs.purpose: Micro mono figure at 0.6875rem = 11px, the mono floor: every .paper-edge, agenda and session slip edges, FAQ question numbers, avatar counts, kit file sizes, the footer folio.

note-sm.purpose: Special Elite tells: roles, captions, tape labels, row metadata (the ticket alt price and edge, the speaker role, agenda room notes). Sentence case, tracking 0, line-height 1.45; 0.85rem is the floor.

note.purpose: Special Elite tells: .eyebrow, a speaker print's talk, form labels and errors, the sheet kicker, nav meta, the FAQ index label. A label made of words is this voice, never mono.

action.purpose: Bebas speaks: the text action (.action / .btn-ghost), the nav toggle, desktop bar and footer links, Sheet close, speaker social links, the session filters, Clear. Caps, line-height 1, no glyph.

cta.purpose: The label on a red button (cta-label = action(--fs-cta)): white Bebas at 1.5rem = 24px, the regular-weight large-text line where white on #F11000 (4.36:1) clears AA; the header Tickets, every .btn-primary, the newsletter submit. Never shrink it. Also the size of the agenda room filter and the FAQ index.

title-sm.purpose: Bebas 1.45rem: speaker print names <=720px, mobile record titles, press-kit variant names.

subpage.purpose: The subpage <h1> in SubpageHero: Bebas --fs-subpage clamp(5rem, 13vw, 12.5rem), one per page, type-first, beside a factual lede and at most one print.

section.purpose: The poster section head (.head-rule-title): Bebas --fs-section clamp(4.5rem, 12vw, 12.5rem), on space, never on a rule. Also the footer wordmark and the /venue closer title.

card-title.purpose: Bebas 1.95rem: the speaker name on a print (line-height 0.92), the live slip's Buy label, the teaser's "All speakers".

body-lg.purpose: Special Elite 1.15rem / 1.6: the .head-rule note in soft ink (max 30ch), subpage ledes, footnotes, a session slip's title.

shadows.name: paper-shadow
shadows.purpose: A print, slip or card lifted off the black table: one deep drop, one contact shadow. A property of the paper at rest, never a hover state.

shadows.name: print-mount
shadows.purpose: The speaker sheet's photograph well (.print) and the attending card preview only; every other photograph is a paper print.

shadows.name: statement-lift
shadows.purpose: The home statement's legibility lift on the hero photograph (the event print's subtitle carries a second); type on a photograph only, never on the black ground. Recorded as an open point, not a style.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: The standard control transition: buttons, inputs, links; a text action's colour turning accent-hot on hover and focus.

motion.name: field
motion.purpose: The row reach field colour and opacity fade.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: The house arrive curve: sheet entry, row pull.

motion.name: develop
motion.purpose: The signature motion: the speaker print develops from B&W to colour while its link or button is hovered or focused; on /team the colour bleeds from the cursor (0.7s). Every other print stays B&W. With the portrait view transition into the speaker sheet, the only decorative motion. A print's tilt is set, never animated; nothing moves on its own.

motion.name: slip-lift
motion.purpose: An agenda or session slip lifts 3px under the pointer. Recorded as an open point against "nothing slides".

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: A red fill: the header Tickets on every page, then the page's own (the hero's "Get tickets", the live slip's "Buy", the newsletter submit, a closer's primary, /speakers "Get tickets", the brand-manual download, the partnership deck). White Bebas at --fs-cta 24px (brand manual p. 11; AA as large text only, never shrink), tracking 0, no glyph. Hover inverts the fill (to black on a paper card); no lift, no glow.

components.name: Text Action
components.description: The second control, and the last (.action; .btn-ghost draws the same thing for its older callers). Bebas --fs-action caps, tracking 0, no box, no fill, no underline, no glyph; vertical padding only, min-height 2.75rem. Hover and focus turn the label red (--color-accent-hot); nothing moves. On paper it takes --paper-ink (the slip's "Company pays" draws a red underline instead of turning red). Every "see all", way-across, EndLine link and the ticket head's "Request a company invoice" are this.

components.name: Section Head
components.description: The section head (.head-rule, the class keeps its old name): a poster-scale Bebas --fs-section title left and, on its baseline, at most one note (Special Elite --fs-body-lg, line-height 1.6, soft ink, max 30ch) or the section's text actions right. No rule: space closes it (margin-bottom clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.5rem)). The note carries a fact ("24 confirmed. Times in CET.", "Ten editions since 2015.", the invoice route on Tickets) or is left off. Tickets, Speakers, Past editions, Partners on /; "Every talk", "The route", "In the news" on subpages.

components.name: Paper Print
components.description: The darkroom primitive (.paper, .paper-photo, .paper-edge, .tape, .grease in BaseLayout.scss). A photograph is a print: a white-at-94% border (0.65rem on three sides, open at the foot), the paper shadow, a tilt from --tilt-1 0.8deg to --tilt-3 2.2deg and never more (clamped to --tilt-1 <=720px); inside it the black well with the image in grayscale(1) contrast(1.1); under it the mono edge (a frame or sheet number, a date or time) in dim paper ink. A tape overlaps its top edge with a typed label. One red grease-pencil stroke per section marks the one thing that matters. The same paper carries slips and cards with no photograph (ticket slips, agenda and session slips, FAQ questions, index cards, the newsletter card).

components.name: Eyebrow
components.description: A plain typewriter note where a list has no poster head: the NextStepList head, the /thank-you calendar stub, a Closer eyebrow, the invite alias. Special Elite --fs-note, sentence case, no tracking, no decoration, no trailing hairline; never uppercased, never mono.

components.description: The ruled list that is left: the rows in the speaker and session sheets and the NextStep rows on /404 and the thank-you pages. Each row closes on a 1px 13%-white rule and opens on --field-step of air; hierarchy is type scale and ink. A row that IS the control (a speaker row in the session sheet) paints a full-bleed red reach field on hover and every ink goes full black. Lists on the black table elsewhere are paper slips, not rows.

components.name: Ticket Slip
components.description: One paper ticket slip per wave under the "Tickets" head (whose note is the invoice route). The wave on sale is the big slip, tilted --tilt-1: the wave name Bebas --fs-h2, the price JetBrains Mono 500 at --fs-h2, the other variant's price as a note line ("Company funded 1 452 Kč"), the state as a note in dim paper ink ("On sale.", the deadline), a perforation of punched holes through to the table, then the VAT line and the mono event date left and the red Buy (--fs-card-title) and the paper-ink "Company pays" right. A spent wave is a small slip tilted -tilt-3, its paper a shade darker, crossed out by the grease pencil; a wave still to come is a small plain slip. Phones stack the slips full width.

components.description: The text field: a 5.5% white plate with the control-edge boundary, turning accent-hot on focus. The label is a typewriter note (a word, so never mono). Keyboard focus adds the ring tight against the edge.

components.name: Speaker Print
components.description: Every speaker as a paper print on the black table, in running order (start time, then room; then untimed; then hosts), the same print on / (links; eight, the last cell "N / All speakers") and on /speakers (buttons opening the sheet; the print's photo morphs into the sheet's; the last cell "Full agenda" and the red "Get tickets"). A print: a tape over its top edge naming the room, the 4:5 B&W portrait, the Bebas name at --fs-card-title in paper ink, the role as a note clamped to two lines, the talk as a note, "With ..." for co-speakers, and the mono edge "NN / NN" and the CET start. Tilts cycle so neighbours never match. Reached, the name turns red and the portrait develops to colour. The opening keynote is the large print (two columns by two rows) with red grease corners. Four columns (three on /speakers <=1100px), two <=720px, where every print, the keynote too, is equal.

components.name: Agenda Slip
components.description: /agenda as slips on the table. Over it a bar: the room filter (Bebas words, red when on) and "All times Prague (CET)". Desktop: rooms are columns under their tapes, a mono gutter names each start; the grid is not to scale (one row per moment something starts or ends). Each talk is a paper slip from its start line to its end line, barely tilted: a mono caps edge (time range, track), the title in Special Elite --fs-body, the speakers in Bebas, and a "Live now" flag behind a red dot. A break is a quiet typewriter line across the rooms; a "Slot open" is a dashed outline; the lounge is one dark block all day. Phones (<=720px): one list grouped by start time, each slip taped with its room.

narrative.northStar: Noir, but loud — the darkroom: prints on a black table in three voices
narrative.overview: A film-noir darkroom: a single black table, white ink, greys only as white at an opacity, and the photographs and the facts that travel with them laid on it as paper (white at 94%, black ink): prints with a white border and a mono edge, ticket slips, agenda and session slips, index cards, all set down by hand at a small tilt, labelled with strips of tape, numbered like frames, and marked with one red grease-pencil stroke per section. Section heads are poster-scale Bebas on space, never on a rule; subpages open on type with at most one print. Red is a fill (the header Tickets and each page's own button), a grease stroke or a state, never running text and never a ground. Two controls and no third: the red fill and the Bebas text action, neither carrying a glyph. Three voices: Bebas speaks (headlines and actions), Special Elite tells (prose and every label made of words), JetBrains Mono records (figures). Nothing glows, nothing moves on its own; the speaker prints develop to colour under the pointer.
keyCharacteristics: One theme, and it is dark: a black table
Photographs are paper prints; facts that travel with them are paper slips and cards in the same paper and ink
Paper and tape are white at an opacity, ink on paper is black at an opacity; no cream
Prints tilt by hand, alternating, never past --tilt-3; on a phone every print is equal and barely tilted
Tape labels; one red grease-pencil stroke marks one thing per section
Poster-scale section heads on space; subpages open on type with at most one print
Two controls site-wide: the red fill and the Bebas text action; no arrow glyphs, a hover is red
Three voices: Bebas speaks, Special Elite tells, JetBrains Mono records figures
Three faces: Bebas Neue, Special Elite, JetBrains Mono (brand manual v1.0)
No glow: hover and live states are flat colour changes; the paper shadow is the paper's, not a hover
No icon library; the only text glyph left is the Sheet's Close ✕

rules.name: The Darkroom Rule
rules.body: Photographs are paper prints on the black table (.paper, .paper-photo, .paper-edge): a white-at-94% border, the paper shadow, a mono edge. A fact that travels with them (a ticket, a talk, an inbox, a question, the newsletter) is a slip or card in the same paper and ink (--paper-ink black, --paper-ink-dim black 66%). A tape (white 82%, a typed note) labels a print or a group. One red grease-pencil stroke per section marks the one thing that matters: a ringed figure, a crossed-out wave, the keynote's corners. Prints tilt by a fraction or a step of --tilt-1 0.8deg / --tilt-2 1.4deg / --tilt-3 2.2deg, alternating so neighbours never match, never past --tilt-3, and at most --tilt-1 under 720px, where every print is equal.

rules.name: The Red Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Brand manual v1.0 (p. 08-09): three colours, #000000, #FFFFFF, #F11000; greys only as white or black at an opacity (panels, ink, paper and tape are rgba()). Red marks details (a dot, 1-2 headline words, the year, CTA words, a grease-pencil stroke, a text action under the pointer) and, as a large area, only red buttons and the row reach field. No red ground: every closer, the /partners CTA and the newsletter sit on black. Never running text (in-prose links are white on a red underline), never a wash, never another accent hue. On paper, red is a stroke, a dot or a button: #F11000 on --paper is about 3.8:1, so small text on paper stays in paper ink. One red mark per list (manual p. 11). Errors stay red: a state.

rules.name: The Size Not Dimming Rule
rules.body: On red, hierarchy comes from size. On flat #F11000 (chips, the reach field) ink is #000000 at full opacity (4.8:1); 85% black is for control boundaries only; white only for large type (4.36:1). A red button's label is white Bebas at --fs-cta 1.5rem = 24px (cta-label = action(--fs-cta)), the regular-weight large-text line; Bebas has no bold, so the size carries it, never smaller. Red type on black (the ticket state word) is 4.82:1.

rules.name: The Two Controls Rule
rules.body: Every action is the page's one red fill (.btn-primary: white Bebas caps at --fs-cta on #F11000, inverted on hover) or the Bebas text action (.action / .btn-ghost: --fs-action caps, tracking 0, no box, no fill, no underline, vertical padding only, min-height 2.75rem, the label turning --color-accent-hot on hover and focus). No arrow glyph anywhere: the → after a link and the ↗ off-site marker are deleted, because a glyph renders differently on every system and the label names the destination. A boxed secondary, an underlined standalone link or a second filled colour is a third control and does not ship. The header's Tickets is a red button on every page; the hero's "Get tickets", the live slip's Buy and the newsletter submit are the home page's own (the count is an open point). A filter is a Bebas word, red when on.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Bebas speaks: headlines and actions (display(), row-title(), action(), cta-label). Special Elite tells: prose and every label made of words (prose(), note()): eyebrows, roles, captions, tape labels, form labels, errors, status words, the ticket state, sheet kicker, nav meta, the footer. JetBrains Mono records: figures only (mono()): prices, times, frame and sheet numbers on a print's edge, counts, codes, the footer folio. Mono never sets a word-label; the darkroom edges and agenda flags that still set words in mono caps are an open point. note() is sentence case, tracking 0, line-height 1.45, floored at --fs-note-sm; action() is Bebas caps at --fs-action, tracking 0, line-height 1.

rules.name: The Poster Head Rule
rules.body: A section opens on .head-rule (the class keeps its old name): the section's plain name in Bebas --fs-section (clamp(4.5rem, 12vw, 12.5rem)) left and, on its baseline, at most one note (Special Elite --fs-body-lg, soft ink, max 30ch) or the section's text actions right. No rule under it: the ruled head made every section read as a table. Space closes it. A subpage title sets at --fs-subpage in SubpageHero, beside a factual lede and at most one print. Headings are literal: no puns.

rules.name: The Head Note Is A Fact Rule
rules.body: A head note carries a fact the visitor needs, never a label of the section's own contents: Speakers ("N confirmed. Times in CET."), Past editions ("Ten editions since 2015."), Tickets (the invoice route, a quiet side door beside the poster title), "Every talk" (how to search), "The route" (the train and the walk), "In the news" (where the press kit is). Partners takes its two text actions in the note's place. A note that only names what follows is filler and is left off.

rules.name: The Structural Rule Rule
rules.body: Space and paper part the page, not lines. A line is drawn only under a .field row (the sheets, the NextStep lists), in data tables, as a control boundary, as an in-prose underline, as a progress spine, as the dashed outline of a place still empty (an open agenda slot, the end of "Every talk"), as the short mark between the desktop bar's two link groups, and as the cookie banner's edge. Never a rule under a section head, a divider between sections, a line above the hero's facts line, a ruled readout, a rule down an agenda room column, or a box drawn round a partner mark. The footer opens on space.

rules.name: The Poster Scale Rule
rules.body: One --fs-subpage title per subpage. Section heads at --fs-section; a poster title a step under them at --fs-display; Closer titles at --fs-h2; a compact head on a card at --fs-head. The home statement sets at --fs-hero, under the section heads below it (an open point).

rules.name: The One Red Word Rule
rules.body: The red accent word and the closing full stop belong to the home hero statement (and the invite title). Every subpage title carries neither; section heads and every Closer title are plain white.

rules.name: The No Fake Styles Rule
rules.body: font-synthesis: none. One weight per face (JetBrains Mono loads 400 and 500; 500 for the ticket slip price and the clipping headline) and no italic, so prose emphasis is ink (strong steps up to --color-text). Czech letters Special Elite lacks fall to JetBrains Mono.

rules.name: The Motion Answers A Change Rule
rules.body: No scroll reveal, no per-section entrance, no page-entry animation: the hero lands still. Nothing moves on its own: no ticker, no countdown, no rotor, no marquee; the contact sheet is still; the agenda's live dot is static. One signature motion: the speaker print develops from high-contrast B&W (manual p. 13) to colour while reached; on /team the colour bleeds from the cursor. A print's tilt is set, never animated. A text action's hover is a colour change (the 3px lift on agenda and session slips is an open point). Hover painting only under (hover: hover).

rules.name: The Bebas Setting Rule
rules.body: Bebas sets uppercase at line-height 0.9-1.0 and tracking 0 (manual p. 10): --lh-display 0.9, --track-display 0, row-title() and action() line-height 1. No Bebas rule carries its own letter-spacing (the desktop bar and footer links are an open point); no text-shadow on the black ground (the home statement and the event print's subtitle, both on a photograph, are an open point).

rules.name: The Mono Grid Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono tracks at 0.1-0.2em (manual p. 10). A figure has no case to force (the uppercase paper edges, agenda flags, hero frame stamp and folio are an open point). mono() floors effective tracking at 0.1em under --track-scale; notes and actions carry no tracking and do not move on a phone. Speaker names on the agenda and session slips set in Bebas, where manual p. 11 asks for Special Elite: an open point.

rules.name: The Logo Never Shrinks Rule
rules.body: Official files only (manual p. 03-07). The header logo is a fixed 190px box (180px digital minimum) and the brand never shrinks; the bar tightens on phones and drops its red Tickets under 380px instead. No opacity change on logo hover; nothing darkens the logo. No logo on the home hero: the bar carries the mark. The footer's typeset "DevFest.cz" sign-off is an open point.

rules.name: The Recipe Rule
rules.body: Every font declaration goes through _type.scss (note, action, cta-label, mono, display, row-title, prose, hairline-link); every font-size through the ramp.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: No glow anywhere. Hover and live states are flat colour changes: an inverted fill for the red button, a red label for the text action, a border or ink change for rows and fields. The paper shadow is the paper's, at rest; it never grows on hover.

rules.name: The Size By Tier Rule
rules.body: Partner logos sit on the black table with no tile, border or plate of the wall's own, each in its original colours (brand manual p. 15); dark-ink masters on a tilted paper card. Each tier is labelled with a strip of tape. The tier's reference box sets the size (CELLS: Platinum 600x300, Diamond 330x190, Gold 260x150, Silver 210x120, Community and Media 180x100 px); opticalBox() gives every mark in a tier the same ink area, handed to CSS as --logo-w. /partners scales each tier up through TIER_SCALE and lines Diamond and Gold up in columns; the home wall uses the boxes as they are with a --logo-scale per tier. Media stays on /partners.

rules.name: The End Line Rule
rules.body: Each page ends on its one next step. A Closer, on the black ground, ends a page that asks for a decision (agenda, workshops, venue, invite); /speakers ends on the last cell of its grid ("Full agenda", "Get tickets"). A page that asks for none ends on an EndLine (one lede line and one text action) or on its content (legal pages, 404's step list, /contact's press kit, /team's "Want to help next year?").

rules.name: The One Print Rule
rules.body: The detective key art is the home hero's alone: on the right of the hero, fading in from the left, with the statement, the facts and the red fill set over it. A subpage opens on type with at most one print: /partners, /venue and /contact each take one documentary photograph as a 4:3 paper print beside the title; /speakers, /agenda and every other subpage carry none. Beyond the hero, / carries the event print, the speaker prints and the "Past editions" contact sheet with its enlargement.

rules.name: The Earned Noir Rule
rules.body: Noir wordplay is spent in a few earned places: the home hero statement, the 404 "Nothing filed under that", and at most one closer line per page. Every section and page title says plainly what it is ("Tickets", "Speakers", "Past editions", "Partners", "Newsletter", "Agenda", "Every talk", "The team", "Questions", "Contact", "Become a partner"); a head note is a fact or absent. The case dressing is the darkroom's: frame numbers and dates on a print's edge, the hero's "Frame 01" stamp, the footer's folio. No triads, no em-dash chains, no hype words.

rules.name: The One Date Format Rule
rules.body: Event facts come from src/lib/event.ts: doors 08:00, keynote 09:00, close 19:00, afterparty to 23:00. "30 October 2026" in running copy, "30 Oct 2026" in mono facts, never "October 30"; 24-hour HH:MM; British "programme".

dos: Do use global primitives by class name (.band, .head-rule, .paper, .paper-photo, .paper-edge, .tape, .grease, .eyebrow, .display, .btn-primary, .action).
Do set a photograph as a .paper print with its edge, and a fact that travels with it as a paper slip or card in the same paper and ink.
Do alternate tilts so neighbours never match, and keep every print under --tilt-3 (under --tilt-1 on a phone).
Do open a section on the poster .head-rule with the section's name, and a note only where it carries a fact.
Do spend one grease stroke per section, on the one thing that matters.
Do set every label made of words with note() and every action with action(); keep mono() for figures.
Do give every data-backed page a .fallback-note.
Do use --field-border (≥3:1) for a control boundary on black and --paper-ink on paper.
Do add a prefers-reduced-motion opt-out to every animation.
Do use .action for every "see all", way-across or secondary link, and the hairline-link mixin for a link inside running text.
Do render every partner mark through partnerLogo() and the partner-logo() recipe, so its tier's reference box sets its size.
donts: Don't add a fourth font, an icon package, Tailwind or CSS-in-JS.
Don't set paragraphs in #F11000, add a second red or any other accent hue, or use --color-error as an accent.
Don't use a cream hex for paper; paper and tape are white at an opacity.
Don't set small red text on paper; a stroke, a dot or a button carries the red there.
Don't tilt a print past --tilt-3, or two neighbours the same way by the same step.
Don't add a third control: no boxed or outlined secondary, no underlined standalone link, no second filled colour.
Don't put an arrow or off-site glyph on a link or a button; the label names the destination.
Don't set a word-label in JetBrains Mono, uppercase a note, or track a note or an action.
Don't draw a rule under a section head or between sections; space parts the page.
Don't paint the reach field on :focus; focus draws a ring.
Don't introduce a prefers-color-scheme block for a single component.
Don't use translateX on the red reach field; the pull belongs to the wash.
Don't give a head a note that only names what follows; a note is a fact or nothing.
Don't put a mood eyebrow ('Be there', 'Join us') on a closer; an eyebrow carries a fact or nothing.
Don't paint a red ground under a closer, a form or a section; the red on a screen is a button.
Don't spend a second grease stroke or a second red mark in a list.
Don't add a glow to a hover or live state, or grow the paper shadow on hover.
Don't draw a tile, border or plate of the wall's own behind a partner logo; the tier's box carries the rank.
Don't set a mono figure under 11px (--fs-label-xs is the floor) or a note under --fs-note-sm.
Don't shrink, dim or overlay the logo; change the layout instead.
Don't set a label on red smaller than --fs-cta.
Don't put more than one print on a subpage hero.
Don't add anything that moves on its own: no rotor, ticker, countdown or marquee.
Don't spend noir wordplay on a plain title; name the page.
